newsitem.title: USA: Ohio soybean, corn plantings above average pace.
newsitem.headline: Ohio soybean, corn plantings above average pace.

text.p: Soybean plantings in Ohio stayed above the average pace during the week ended Sunday and corn emergence was also above average, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.
Soybean plantings were 74 percent complete, compared with the average pace of 69 percent and last year's 23 percent, the report said.
Seventy-six percent of the corn crop had emerged versus the five-year average of 65 percent and last week's pace of 57 percent. The Ohio corn crop was 96 percent planted, according to the report.
The corn crop was rated 56 percent good to excellent, 32 percent fair, 10 percent poor and two percent very poor.
Forty-nine percent of the soybean crop had emerged compared to last week's figure of seven percent.

Winter wheat was rated 12 percent excellent, 44 percent good, 31 percent fair, 10 percent poor and three percent very poor. Ninety-seven percent of the wheat crop was jointed and twenty-two percent was headed versus the average of 50 percent.
Topsoil moisture levels were 50 percent surplus, 49 percent adequate and one percent short.
